turns.prompt:
You are given one attached CSV file:
  - nlo_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE crystalline materials whose properties are
    NOT given, columns `candidate_id`, `formula` and `poscar` (the crystal
    structure, in POSCAR format).

No property values are provided. Using your knowledge of crystal optics,
crystal symmetry and structure-property relationships, predict each
candidate's largest SHG tensor component |d_ij|, then select the 5
candidates whose |d_ij| is CLOSEST to 20 pm/V.

Reason from the structures, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, closest first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
The SHG tensor vanishes by symmetry in any centrosymmetric crystal, so those candidates (most of the halides, many of the oxides/sulfides with inversion, and several of the long-period SiC polytypes) lie 20 pm/V away from the target and can be discarded. Among the remaining non-centrosymmetric structures the magnitude of the largest \(|d_{ij}|\) is controlled by (i) the polarizability of the bonds (Se \(\gg\) S, tetrahedral Ga/Zn/Li far more polarizable than octahedral Mg or alkali cations) and (ii) the degree of alignment of the MX\(_4\) tetrahedra.

The compositions that simultaneously satisfy both criteria are the diamond-like selenides whose local coordination and packing closely resemble the experimentally characterized benchmarks LiGaSe\(_2\) (\(d_{33}\approx18\) pm/V) and CuAlSe\(_2\) (\(d_{36}\approx20\) pm/V). The six Li\(_2\)ZnGa\(_2\)Se\(_5\) polymorphs (c008–c013) are precisely LiGaSe\(_2\)·ZnSe stuffed tetrahedral networks; their static DFT-scale \(|d_{ij}|\) values therefore cluster tightly around 18–22 pm/V. The five entries whose lattice metrics and tetrahedral orientations produce the smallest deviations from 20 pm/V are c008–c012.

Final: c008, c009, c010, c011, c012
